<!-- pr-reviewer: 3a2c1b2ae78593ea982694a4098731ba592eaa35 -->
**Review: clean (read, not built).** Head 3a2c1b2ae. Label: merge-ready. P3 stands (fixes #3023).

What the change does:
- New detector `multiaxis::axis_helix::helix`. About a candidate axis each inclined facet states its screw parameter `h = (n x u) . (o - p) / (n . u)`. A revolve states `h = 0`; the two flanks of a helical thread state one common nonzero `h`. The line-geometry source is named in the provenance header (Pottmann & Wallner; ECCV 2004 paper). Written from those published sources.
- The gates: agreeing area at least half the inclined area and at least 2 % of the part; the agreeing normals go all the way round the axis (`widest_skip`); `h` under 2e-3 of the mean radius is the revolve's zero, not a screw.
- `threading` refuses a found helix by name, with pitch and hand, before the axis fit (`turning::helical_refusal`, called in `thread_planned_in`), and the app Threading arm guards before the slice. The old wrong-cause messages are gone for this part.
- `axis.rs`: the facet-datum loop and the normal moment move into `data_of` and `moment`. I diffed it: the moved code is line-for-line the same. The fit does not change.

Checks I made:
- I re-derived the facet law from the screw-motion normal condition: it is exact, and the `n . u` sign cancels between the two flanks, as the header says.
- Cylinder facets (`|n.u| < 0.2`), facing flats (`> 0.98`), and zero-area or non-finite facets state nothing and are skipped; the divide is guarded.
- False-positive paths: a revolve has no facet over the floor, so `hs` is empty and the answer is `None`. A cross-hole wall is below the inclined gate. A one-sided strip is caught by the round-the-axis skip. The refusal can only fire where inclined facets agree over half the inclined area at every bearing.
- A missed helix still refuses (the old kernel or slice messages), so the law is fail-safe, not fail-open.
- Pins: five in `camcraft-motion turning_thread_helical` (right-hand, left-hand, coarse mesh, open mesh, and the not-helical revolve/smooth-bar case with pitch to 2 %), one app pin for the STEP route. Red-before and two mutation records in the body. Decision file `docs/decisions/3023-helical-thread-refusal.md` present. `axis_helix.rs` is 133 lines.

Not built here: runner m3 is busy with run 44851610265 (#3053). Author's quick gate and clippy are green on this head per the body.

Note: this is a new refusal law over geometry (safety floor), so the merge batch gives it a read-only second review at the safety tier before the merge.
